style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A short psalm about where to run. David's friends -- frightened, sensible, faithless -- tell him to flee like a bird to his mountain: the archers have bent their bows and fitted the arrow to shoot from the dark, and when the foundations are demolished what can a righteous man do? He answers with the one thing they left out. The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD's throne is in heaven; His eyes see and His eyelids narrow like an assayer's over the children of men. That gaze tests the righteous and hates the lover of violence; it will rain fire and sulfur and scorching wind into the cup of the wicked, and it loves righteous deeds. So the psalm ends not with a hiding place but with a face: the upright will see His. He had already said in the first line where he had taken refuge, and it was not a mountain.

1.text: For the choir director. Of David. In the LORD I have taken refuge; how can you say to my soul, 'Flee like a bird to your mountain'?
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm of David. In the LORD [YHWH] put I my trust [chasah -- take refuge]: how say [amar] you to my soul [nephesh], Flee [nud -- flit, wander] as a bird [tsippor] to your mountain [har]?
1.notes: ba-YHWH chasiti (H3068, H2620): in the LORD I have TAKEN REFUGE -- the perfect tense, a settled fact, and the whole answer to the advice that follows; ekh tomeru le-naphshi nudi harkhem tsippor (H559, H5315, H5110, H2022, H6833): how can you tell my soul, 'flit to your mountain, bird'? -- the counsel of frightened friends, sensible and faithless. David's refuge is a Person, not a hill.

2.text: For look, the wicked bend the bow; they have fitted their arrow to the string, so that out of the dark they may shoot at the upright in heart.
2.amp: For, lo, the wicked [rasha] bend [darak -- tread, bend] their bow, they make ready [kun] their arrow [chets] upon the string [yether -- cord], that they may privily ['in darkness', ophel, the KJV margin] shoot [yarah] at the upright [yashar] in heart [leb].
2.notes: ki hinneh ha-reshaim yidrekhun qeshet (H7563, H1869): the wicked TREAD the bow -- the big war-bow was strung with the foot; konenu chitsam al-yeter (H3559, H2671, H3499): arrow fitted to the string -- lirot bemo-ophel le-yishre-leb (H3384, H652, H3477, H3820): to shoot in the dark, the margin's literal, at the straight of heart. The friends' case: the archers are ready and you cannot see them.

3.text: If the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?
3.amp: If the foundations be destroyed [haras -- torn down], what can the righteous [tsaddiq] do [paal]?
3.notes: ki ha-shatot yeharesun (H2040): when the shatot, the foundations -- of law, of order, of the social house -- are demolished; tsaddiq mah-paal (H6662, H6466): the righteous one, what has he done, or what can he do? Read as the last word of the counselors (flee, the structure is gone) or as David's own question; either way verse 4 is the answer, and it does not mention the foundations.

4.text: The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD, His throne is in heaven; His eyes see, His eyelids test the children of men.
4.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is in His holy [qodesh] temple [hekal -- palace], the LORD'S [YHWH] throne [kisse] is in heaven [shamayim]: His eyes [ayin] behold [chazah], His eyelids [aphaph] try [bachan -- test, assay], the children [ben] of men [adam].
4.notes: YHWH be-hekal qodsho, YHWH ba-shamayim kiso (H3068, H1964, H6944, H8064, H3678): two facts that outlast any collapsed foundation -- the LORD is in His holy palace, and His throne is in heaven. enav yechezu aphappav yibchanu bene adam (H5869, H2372, H6079, H974, H1121, H120): His eyes see, His EYELIDS test -- the narrowed gaze of an assayer -- the sons of men. Habakkuk 2:20 begins its silence with this line.

5.text: The LORD tests the righteous, but the wicked and the lover of violence His soul hates.
5.amp: The LORD [YHWH] tries [bachan -- tests] the righteous [tsaddiq]: but the wicked [rasha] and him that loves [ahab] violence [chamas] His soul [nephesh] hates [sane].
5.notes: YHWH tsaddiq yibchan (H3068, H6662, H974): the LORD ASSAYS the righteous -- the same bachan as verse 4, the refiner's test that proves the metal (cf. Psalm 66:10); ve-rasha ve-oheb chamas saneah naphsho (H7563, H157, H2555, H8130, H5315): the wicked, the lover of chamas, violence, His soul hates. Testing for the righteous, hatred for the violent: the same gaze from heaven does both.

6.text: He will rain snares on the wicked -- fire and sulfur and a scorching wind will be the portion of their cup.
6.amp: Upon the wicked [rasha] He shall rain snares [pach], fire [esh] and brimstone [gophrith -- sulfur], and an horrible ['a burning tempest', zalaphah, the KJV margin] tempest [ruach -- wind]: this shall be the portion [menah -- allotment] of their cup [kos].
6.notes: yamter al-reshaim pachim esh ve-gophrith (H7563, H6341, H784, H1614): He rains pachim -- snares, or, as many read the word, coals -- fire and sulfur, Sodom's weather (Genesis 19:24); ve-ruach zilaphot menat kosam (H7307, H2152, H4521, H3563): and a scorching wind, the margin's 'burning tempest', the portion of their cup. The cup is Psalm 16:5's word for one's allotted lot -- here poured for the wicked (cf. Psalm 75:8).

7.text: For the LORD is righteous and He loves righteous acts; the upright will look upon His face.
7.amp: For the righteous [tsaddiq] LORD [YHWH] loves [ahab] righteousness [tsedaqah -- righteous deeds]; His countenance [panim -- face] does behold [chazah] the upright [yashar].
7.notes: ki-tsaddiq YHWH tsedaqot aheb (H6662, H3068, H6666, H157): the righteous LORD loves righteousnesses -- the plural, righteous acts; yashar yechezu phanemo (H3477, H2372, H6440): the KJV reads it 'his countenance doth behold the upright', the WEB 'the upright shall see his face'. The Hebrew allows both, and the psalm has earned both: the eyes that tested (v. 4) are the face the upright will finally see (cf. Matthew 5:8; Revelation 22:4). The bird did not need the mountain.
